TUTORME

fake news check

Your tutor against disinformation: the techniques that spread it, and the ways your own mind falls for it.

Android Free · no ads · no purchases Nine languages No account, no server

What it does

Spot fake news: fact-checking with real sources and daily critical thinking.

Fact-check

Type the claim you read or heard. The app goes looking for evidence and gives you the verdict, the sources — one by one, tap to open, each one says what kind of source it is — and the techniques it recognised in that sentence. With the detailed analysis you can ask about one part only.

Today's lesson

Five minutes, one topic at a time. Not canned lessons: they are created for you, one at a time. Each leaves you something to remember and a link to what you have already seen. Get it wrong and the app explains why that mistake is so common.

Debate

The app argues a position, you argue for or against it. Nothing pre-packaged here either: the claim is written on the spot, and you won't meet the same one twice.

When the evidence isn't enough you won't get a flat "true" or "false": the app says it can't be verified. Learning to recognise that is half the work.

See it

Nine languages, properly

It isn't just a translated interface: lessons, debates and fact-checks are created in your language, and when the app looks for evidence it searches in your language too — not only in English. On a local story that is the difference between finding the debunk and missing it.

It adapts to you, quietly

From the basics — who says so, when did it happen — up to cognitive biases and rhetorical techniques. No level on display, no score to defend: the app changes pace by itself.

For everyone

Dyslexia-friendly typeface, adjustable text size, high contrast, light or dark theme.

No interruptions

No purchases, no "pro" version, no subscription. Nothing that gets in your way while you are reading or answering.

Your data stays yours

No account, no sign-up, no profile. What you do stays on your phone: a server of ours does not exist. No tracking.

Signing in with Google

The app asks for one permission only: its own private app-data folder on your Google Drive, where it saves an encrypted backup of your settings and of how far you got. It cannot see, open or change any other file in your Drive, and the developer has no access to your Drive.

Back on any phone

Save an encrypted copy to Google Drive or to a file: your settings and progress come back when you reinstall the app, on this phone or another one.

Worth knowing. You need a connection: lessons and debates are created on the spot, and fact-checking goes out to look for sources. You start from a written claim, not from a link. And the last word is yours: the app shows you the sources, it doesn't decide for you.
